title: Machine Learning
text:
Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that trains statistical models on data.
Deep learning uses neural networks with many layers to learn hierarchical representations.
Supervised learning trains a model on labeled examples to predict outcomes on new data.
Gradient descent optimizes model parameters by following the negative gradient of a loss function.
Convolutional neural networks are widely used for image classification tasks.
Overfitting occurs when a model learns noise in the training data instead of general patterns.
Reinforcement learning trains an agent to maximize reward through trial and error in an environment.
Transformers use self-attention to model relationships between tokens in a sequence.
Cross-validation splits data into folds to estimate how a model generalizes to unseen data.

title: Neuroscience
text:
Neurons in the human brain communicate through electrochemical signals across synapses.
Biological neural networks in the brain adapt their connections through synaptic plasticity.
The hippocampus plays a central role in forming new long-term memories.
Neurotransmitters such as dopamine and serotonin regulate mood and motivation in the brain.
The cerebral cortex is responsible for higher-order functions like reasoning and language.
Long-term potentiation strengthens synaptic connections when neurons fire together repeatedly.
The brain's visual cortex processes information from the retina in a hierarchy of stages.
Sleep is thought to consolidate memories by replaying neural activity from the day.
Neuroplasticity allows the adult brain to reorganize itself by forming new neural connections.

title: Roman History
text:
The Roman Empire was one of the largest empires in ancient history, spanning three continents.
Rome was founded in 753 BC according to ancient Roman tradition and legend.
Julius Caesar was a Roman general and statesman who played a critical role in the fall of the Republic.
The fall of the Western Roman Empire in 476 AD marked the end of ancient Rome.
Roman legions built an extensive network of roads connecting the empire's provinces.
The Roman Senate was an assembly of the elite that advised Roman magistrates and consuls.
Roman aqueducts carried fresh water into cities across the empire using gravity alone.
The Colosseum in ancient Rome hosted gladiatorial games for tens of thousands of spectators.
Roman law codified in the Twelve Tables influenced legal systems for centuries afterward.

title: Roman Catholic
text:
The Roman Catholic Church traces its leadership to the papacy based in Vatican City.
The Pope is the Bishop of Rome and the leader of the worldwide Roman Catholic Church.
Roman Catholic doctrine holds seven sacraments as central to religious practice.
The Second Vatican Council in the 1960s reformed many Roman Catholic liturgical practices.
Roman Catholic cathedrals across Europe display centuries of religious architecture.
The Catechism of the Roman Catholic Church summarizes core beliefs and moral teachings.
Roman Catholic monasteries preserved classical texts throughout the medieval period.
Canon law governs the internal discipline of the Roman Catholic Church.
Roman Catholic religious orders such as the Jesuits focus on education and missionary work.

title: Solar Power
text:
Solar power converts sunlight directly into electricity using photovoltaic panels.
Solar panel efficiency has improved significantly as photovoltaic cell technology has advanced.
Large-scale solar farms generate renewable electricity across thousands of acres of land.
Rooftop solar installations let homeowners generate their own electricity from sunlight.
Solar inverters convert direct current from panels into alternating current for the electrical grid.
Battery storage paired with solar power allows electricity use after the sun sets.
Concentrated solar power uses mirrors to focus sunlight and generate heat for turbines.
Government subsidies have accelerated the adoption of residential solar power systems.
Solar power is one of the fastest-growing sources of renewable electricity worldwide.

title: Astronomy
text:
The solar system consists of the Sun and the planets, moons, and asteroids that orbit it.
The Sun is a main-sequence star that generates energy through nuclear fusion in its core.
Astronomers use telescopes to observe distant galaxies billions of light-years away.
A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes directly between the Earth and the Sun.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system, with a mass greater than all other planets combined.
Black holes form when massive stars collapse under their own gravity at the end of their lives.
The James Webb Space Telescope observes infrared light from some of the earliest galaxies.
Comets are icy bodies that develop glowing tails as they approach the Sun.
Exoplanets are planets that orbit stars outside our own solar system.

title: Python Language
text:
Python is a high-level programming language widely used in data science and web development.
Python's syntax emphasizes readability, using indentation to define code blocks.
The Python standard library includes modules for file handling, networking, and text processing.
Python supports object-oriented, procedural, and functional programming paradigms.
Popular Python frameworks like Django and Flask are used to build web applications.
NumPy and pandas are core Python libraries for numerical computing and data analysis.
Python's package manager pip installs libraries from the Python Package Index.
Python is dynamically typed, so variable types are checked at runtime rather than compile time.
Virtual environments let Python developers isolate project dependencies from the system installation.

title: Python Snake
text:
Pythons are large, non-venomous constricting snakes found across Africa, Asia, and Australia.
A python kills its prey by constriction, squeezing until the animal can no longer breathe.
The reticulated python is among the longest snake species in the world.
Pythons are ambush predators that can go months between meals after a large kill.
Ball pythons are popular pets due to their calm temperament and manageable size.
Female pythons coil around their eggs to keep them warm until they hatch.
Pythons have heat-sensing pits that let them detect warm-blooded prey in darkness.
Invasive Burmese pythons have disrupted native mammal populations in the Florida Everglades.
Unlike venomous snakes, pythons rely entirely on constriction rather than venom to subdue prey.

title: Chemistry
text:
A chemical reaction rearranges atoms to form new substances with different properties.
The periodic table organizes elements by increasing atomic number and recurring chemical properties.
Covalent bonds form when atoms share electron pairs to complete their outer electron shells.
Acids donate protons in solution, while bases accept them, according to the Bronsted-Lowry theory.
Catalysts speed up chemical reactions without being consumed in the overall process.
Organic chemistry studies carbon-based compounds, including most molecules found in living organisms.
A mole is a unit representing a fixed number of particles, used to count atoms and molecules.
Oxidation-reduction reactions involve the transfer of electrons between chemical species.
Polymers are large molecules made of repeating structural units called monomers.

title: Cooking
text:
Searing meat at high heat creates a browned crust through the Maillard reaction.
Braising combines searing with slow, moist cooking to tenderize tough cuts of meat.
A roux made from flour and fat thickens sauces like bechamel and gravy.
Fermentation uses microorganisms to transform ingredients, as in bread, yogurt, and kimchi.
Blanching vegetables briefly in boiling water helps preserve their color and texture.
Emulsification combines oil and water-based ingredients into a stable mixture, as in mayonnaise.
Resting meat after cooking allows its juices to redistribute before it is sliced.
Caramelization browns sugars at high temperature, producing rich, complex flavors.
Sous vide cooking holds food at a precise low temperature in a sealed bag for even results.
